title: Change events webhook

story.i_want_to: deliver a change's event log to loopctl
story.so_that: a story learns what happened to its change without anyone polling GitHub

rationale: PRD §5. Machine-called endpoint, exempt from the MCP-tool rule like the runner socket.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/change_events/:source_id verifies X-Chg-Signature, an HMAC over "<X-Chg-Timestamp>.<raw body>" with that source's change_events_secret. An unknown source id, a revoked or non-:chg source, a bad signature and a timestamp outside 5 minutes all return the same 401, write nothing, and are logged and counted per source.
An event is idempotent on (tenant_id, repo, change_id, event_seq): a redelivery returns 200 with duplicate: true and applies nothing twice.

Events apply in event_seq order per change. An event ahead of a gap is stored and applied when the gap fills; a gap older than 10 minutes enqueues one reconciliation job per change (Oban, unique on change) that pulls the missing events from chg. A bound change whose story is not terminal and that has had no event for 6 hours is pulled the same way, and a pull refused for its signature raises an operator alert.
Every applied event is appended to the tenant audit chain with change_id, event_seq and sha.
The request makes no outbound call. Its operation/2 spec documents the 401, the duplicate answer and the body cap, which one module attribute holds for both the guard and the spec.

An event of a kind the stage mapping does not map (review_requested, check_failed, conflict, ready, or any unknown kind) is recorded, answered 2xx, advances the change's applied event_seq, and moves no stage, so it never leaves a gap.

An event for a source whose chg_root_dispatch_id names a dispatch that is now revoked (or no longer a parentless orchestrator-role root of the tenant) is refused with the same 401 as AC-47.3.1 and writes nothing. US-47.2 judges the root only when a source is written, so a root revoked between writes is caught here, by the same rule (Intake's chg root check), read inside the request's transaction.

test_cases.name: one 401 for every refusal
steps: post to an unknown source id

test_cases.name: gap reconciliation
preconditions: seq 1 and 3 present, seq 2 missing for 11 minutes

test_cases.name: unmapped kind keeps ordering whole
expected_results: seq 3 applies immediately, not held behind seq 2: the change's applied event_seq is 3

technical_notes: The chg client is a behaviour resolved from config (Loopctl.Changes.ChgClient), mocked in test/support/mocks.ex.
Build against PRD §5's wire contract, confirmed on mkreyman/chg#33 (headers, signed strings for POST and the gap-pull GET, envelope, per-kind data).

Event application goes through ONE seam, Loopctl.Changes.EventEffects.apply_event/2, called in event_seq order inside the transaction that holds the change's cursor lock, marks the event applied and appends it to the audit chain. In this story it binds a submitted event's story (PRD §4, Loopctl.Changes.bind_in_tenant_transaction/3) and records every other kind; US-47.4 fills it with the stage mapping.
AC-47.3.7's root check is Loopctl.Intake.hold_chg_source/3: the source and its root read FOR SHARE inside the event's own transaction, by the same rule enrolment uses.
chg-server's base URL is the deployment env var CHG_SERVER_URL (one chg-server serves every enrolled repo); unset, events are still received and applied but nothing is pulled.
